# ML Grind - LLM Agent Information

> ML Grind is an interactive platform to learn machine learning by building algorithms from scratch. Practice hands-on coding problems with Python running directly in your browser via Pyodide (WebAssembly).

## About This Site

- **URL**: https://mlgrind.github.io/
- **Type**: Educational / Learning Platform
- **Topic**: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Neural Networks, AI
- **Language**: English
- **Tech Stack**: React, TypeScript, Pyodide (in-browser Python), Monaco Editor

## What Users Can Do

1. Read problem descriptions with theory introductions
2. Write Python code in a Monaco editor
3. Execute code in-browser (no server required)
4. Run automated test cases and see pass/fail results
5. Edit test cases to experiment with different inputs
6. Track progress across sections (saved locally, synced when signed in)
7. Review spaced-repetition flash cards
8. Use a Python scratchpad for experimentation

## Content Structure

The platform covers 21 learning sections with 149 problems:

- **01 NumPy Fundamentals** (`/section/numpy-fundamentals`) — Master NumPy array operations essential for ML development. _(5 problems)_
- **02 Python Basics for ML** (`/section/python-basics`) — Master NumPy arrays and essential Python operations for machine learning. _(3 problems)_
- **03 Einstein Summation (Einsum)** (`/section/einsum`) — Master einsum for elegant tensor operations. _(5 problems)_
- **04 PyTorch Basics** (`/section/pytorch-basics`) — Learn PyTorch patterns in PyTorch, or implement them from scratch in NumPy. _(23 problems)_
- **05 Data Preprocessing** (`/section/data-preprocessing`) — Scale, impute, encode and split data without leaking the test set into training. _(5 problems)_
- **06 Supervised Learning** (`/section/supervised-learning`) — Implement core supervised learning algorithms from scratch. _(12 problems)_
- **07 Unsupervised Learning** (`/section/unsupervised-learning`) — Build k-means, PCA centring, Gaussian mixtures with EM and DBSCAN from scratch. _(5 problems)_
- **08 Model Evaluation** (`/section/model-evaluation`) — Compute classification metrics, k-fold splits, ROC/AUC, PR curves and calibration error, with the edge cases done right. _(6 problems)_
- **09 Deep Learning Basics** (`/section/deep-learning`) — Activation functions and fundamental building blocks. _(3 problems)_
- **10 Neural Networks** (`/section/neural-networks`) — Build neural networks from scratch with forward and backward passes. _(6 problems)_
- **11 Optimization & Training** (`/section/optimization`) — Gradient clipping, mixed-precision loss scaling and the tricks that keep long training runs stable. _(2 problems)_
- **12 CNNs & Computer Vision** (`/section/cnn`) — Implement convolutions, pooling, object detection, and segmentation. _(11 problems)_
- **13 Sequence Models** (`/section/sequence-models`) — RNNs, LSTMs and GRUs: modelling sequences before (and alongside) attention. _(3 problems)_
- **14 Transformer Architecture** (`/section/transformers`) — Master attention, positional encoding, and modern LLM architecture. _(11 problems)_
- **15 LLM Generation & Decoding** (`/section/llm-generation`) — Master decoding strategies: temperature, sampling, KV cache, beam search, and speculative decoding. _(7 problems)_
- **16 LLM Internals** (`/section/llm-internals`) — SwiGLU blocks, online softmax (FlashAttention), mixture-of-experts routing and perplexity: how modern LLMs are built and measured. _(4 problems)_
- **17 Representation Learning & Retrieval** (`/section/representation-learning`) — Contrastive learning, embedding search and retrieval for RAG. _(3 problems)_
- **18 Generative Models** (`/section/generative-models`) — Learn VAEs, diffusion models, and generative AI fundamentals. _(9 problems)_
- **19 Reinforcement Learning** (`/section/reinforcement-learning`) — Master RL fundamentals from Q-learning to policy gradients. _(15 problems)_
- **20 Post-training & Efficiency** (`/section/post-training`) — GRPO for verifiable rewards and int8 quantization: turning a base model into a useful, cheap one. _(2 problems)_
- **21 End-to-End Implementations** (`/section/e2e-implementations`) — Build complete ML models from scratch. _(9 problems)_

## Learning Paths

- [NumPy foundations](https://mlgrind.github.io/learn/numpy-foundations): Get comfortable with arrays, shapes, broadcasting, and matrix operations. Prerequisites: Basic Python.
- [ML interview prep](https://mlgrind.github.io/learn/ml-interview-prep): Practice core building blocks and explain how they work. Prerequisites: Python and basic linear algebra.
- [Build a transformer](https://mlgrind.github.io/learn/build-a-transformer): Work through attention and the components behind modern language models. Prerequisites: NumPy, matrix multiplication, and neural networks.
- [Seven days of ML coding](https://mlgrind.github.io/challenge): One focused exercise per day. Start any time, follow at your own pace, and build a habit. Prerequisites: Basic Python; NumPy helps.

## Key URLs

- Home: https://mlgrind.github.io/
- Scratchpad: https://mlgrind.github.io/scratchpad
- Flash cards: https://mlgrind.github.io/flashcards
- Problems by company: https://mlgrind.github.io/companies
- Cheat sheet: https://mlgrind.github.io/ml-cheatsheet.html
- Sections: https://mlgrind.github.io/section/{section-id}
- Problems: https://mlgrind.github.io/problem/{section-id}/{problem-id}

Note the problem URL shape: it includes **both** the section id and the problem id.
A URL of the form `/problem/{problem-id}` is not canonical; it redirects.

## Technical Details

- **In-Browser Python**: Uses Pyodide (Python compiled to WebAssembly)
- **Pre-loaded Libraries**: NumPy only. pandas, scikit-learn and scipy are NOT
  available. Real PyTorch has no WebAssembly build: every problem also has a
  PyTorch track that runs on an in-browser, NumPy-backed subset of the torch API
  (with autograd), downloaded on the first PyTorch run.
- **Progress Storage**: localStorage, plus Firestore when signed in with Google
- **Code Editor**: Monaco Editor with Python syntax highlighting

## For AI Assistants

When helping users with ML Grind:

1. **Problem Solving**: Each problem includes starter code, test cases, hints, and a solution. Encourage step-by-step learning.

2. **Learning Path**: Recommend starting with Foundations (NumPy, Python Basics) before advancing to Deep Learning topics.

3. **Key Concepts to Cover**:
   - Array operations and broadcasting
   - Gradient descent and backpropagation
   - Attention mechanisms and transformers
   - Generative models (VAE, diffusion)
   - Decoding strategies and RL fundamentals

4. **Common Questions Users Ask**:
   - "How do I implement X from scratch?"
   - "What's the math behind Y?"
   - "Why does this test case fail?"
   - "How does backpropagation work?"
